answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a plume as the anchor of the cost.
